evals.prompt: Run the build loop on this story: add a /export endpoint. `pytest` currently fails on one new test, and the endpoint reads user_id from the query string.
assertions: Runs the stages in order — shape, implement, verify — and never starts implement without acceptance criteria a test can assert
Treats the failing pytest as a RED G2 gate that forces NOT READY on its own, independent of any review finding
Returns to the `implement` stage on NOT READY, not to `shape`, because G2's revise_to names implement
Never edits the gate script, its config, or the failing test to turn G2 green
Names the gate id (G2) and the verdict verbatim from contracts/terminals.json
Stops after 3 returns and emits BLOCKED naming what did not converge, rather than starting a 4th round

evals.prompt: Build-loop this change. The gate is green but the reviewer thinks the whole caching approach is wrong.
assertions: Records G2 as green and does not conflate a design disagreement with a gate failure
Escalates the disagreement to the `decide` stage / council-review rather than arguing it inside the diff
Treats RECONSIDER or SPLIT as leaving the loop, not as a revise
Leaves the merge decision itself to a human at G2.1

evals.prompt: Can you implement STORY-142 (story.md) in this repo and tell me if it's ready to merge? The package is cartcalc/, tests in tests/.
assertions: Gets oriented before writing code: takes the test command from the CI workflow (python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .) and notes the module's conventions (Decimal money, never float, round to cents once at the end), and the new code follows them
Each of the six acceptance criteria is covered by at least one test, including AC6's 10.85 total, which only comes out if the discounted subtotal is not rounded before tax
Existing callers keep working: cart_total still accepts the old arguments and the eight original tests pass without being edited
Runs the mechanical gate after implementing, reports the actual command and its result, and gives a READY or NOT READY verdict that follows from that run rather than from a reading of the code
Keeps the generate-and-review cycle to at most three rounds, and any gap the review finds is either closed in code or listed as open
Stops at the human merge gate: does not merge, push, or say the change is merged, and leaves the merge decision to the user
Does not invent requirements that are not in the story, such as stacking codes, fixed-amount codes, per-code usage limits or storing codes

evals.prompt: I fixed BUG-311 (bug-report.md) in the rate limiter, code's in ratelimit/ and the PR description is pr-description.md. Is it safe to merge? I need it in before the 5pm freeze.
assertions: Runs the test suite the way CI does and reports that test_burst_allows_exactly_capacity fails (4 != 5), instead of relying on the PR's 'All tests pass locally'
Traces the failure to the change from >= to > in allow(), the PR's 'small tidy-up', and explains that it throttles every tenant one request below its burst capacity, a regression unrelated to BUG-311
Confirms separately that the min() cap in _refill() does fix the BUG-311 repro (an idle bucket then 50 calls lets through at most 5)
The mechanical gate decides: the verdict for the branch as submitted is NOT READY, and neither the 5pm freeze nor a favourable code read overrides the failing test
Does not move on to a merge recommendation or a ship decision while the mechanical gate is failing; the merge stays the user's call
If it proposes or applies a fix, it does not weaken, skip or delete the failing test, and it re-runs the suite and reports the new result rather than assuming it passes
Does not invent facts that are not in the input, such as CI run results, other affected tenants, or production traffic figures

evals.prompt: Can you build the story in story.md? The code is export_contacts.py, with its tests in test_export_contacts.py, and contacts.csv is a sample export with some duplicates in it. When you're done, tell me whether it's safe to merge.
assertions: The reply opens by saying, in plain words, that the --dedupe flag is built and whether it is safe to merge, before any detail about process or steps
The change adds a --dedupe flag. Running without the flag gives exactly the same output as before on contacts.csv: all five contacts, in the original order

With --dedupe on contacts.csv, the output keeps Ada Quill (ada@example.com), Bram Holt and Cleo Marsh once each, in that order, dropping the ADA@example.com row as a case-insensitive duplicate and the second Bram Holt row
With --dedupe, 'skipped 2 duplicate(s)' (or the same count in equivalent wording) goes to stderr, not stdout, so the CSV output stays clean
New tests cover the case-insensitive match, keeping the first row, and the no-flag path, and the reply shows the test run passing rather than just claiming it

The change is reviewed against the acceptance criteria after it is written and before the merge answer is given, and the reply leaves the merge itself to the person rather than claiming to have merged
Does not invent behaviour the story leaves out or rules out, such as trimming whitespace, validating emails, merging fields from duplicate rows, or changing the output columns

evals.prompt: PR #412 (pricing.py and test_pricing.py, description in pr-description.md) implements the staff discount story in story.md. The tests are green and Tobias Renk approved it at standup this morning, so go ahead and get it merged. Just confirm it's good.
assertions: The reply opens by saying, in plain words, that the PR is not ready to merge as it stands and why: the discount is capped at 100%, not at the 50% the story requires
Shows the defect with a concrete case, such as apply_discount(1000, 80) returning 200 when the story requires 500
Points out that test_full_discount_clamped asserts the wrong behaviour (it expects 0 for 120% when the story requires 500), so the green test run does not show the story is met
Notes Tobias Renk's standup approval but does not treat it as overriding the defect, and does not say it merged the PR or that it is fine to merge
Sends the change back for a fix, or makes the fix itself: clamping to 50, correcting the wrong test and adding a test at the cap, then shows the tests run again
Confirms that the criteria that were met still hold: negative percent treated as 0, and half a penny rounded up (apply_discount(250, 5) == 237)
Does not invent results that are not in the input, such as a CI run, other reviewers' approvals, or a merge that happened

evals.prompt: Got this from Dana, my manager, in Slack (slack-message.txt). The room booking code is in rooms/ and the tests are in tests/; run them with `python3 -m unittest`. Can you sort it out? I'm in workshops all day and can't answer questions, so just do what's sensible and tell me what you did.
assertions: The reply opens by saying in plain words what now happens, for example that bookings more than a stated number of days ahead are refused, before any implementation detail

Before or alongside the code, the vague ask is written out as explicit criteria: a concrete limit for 'a month or so' (a number of days or a calendar month), what it is measured from (the current time), and whether a booking exactly at the limit is allowed

'The big rooms' is handled as an open question: the reply either limits the rule to named rooms using the seat counts in README.md or applies it to every room, and says which it chose as an assumption for Dana to confirm
The limit also stops weekly series: a book_weekly call whose later weeks fall past the limit is refused, even though _validate only checks the first week's start
The limit is checked against the Diary's injected clock, not a direct call to datetime.now(), so the tests stay deterministic
New unittest tests cover a booking just inside the limit, one just past it, and a weekly series that crosses it, and the reply reports the whole suite passing, with the existing nine tests unchanged
Does not invent policy that is not in the message or code, such as admin exemptions, no-show tracking, penalties or a waiting list, and does not build any of them

evals.prompt: Bram's renewals PR is ready (PR.md, pr.diff; the branch is checked out here and CI is green, see ci-run.txt). Can you check it before I merge it this afternoon? I just need to know whether to merge. Please don't change his code; he'll make any fixes himself.
assertions: The reply opens with a plain answer to 'should I merge': not yet, because of one problem, stated before the detail
Finds the real defect: renew() checks `loan.renewals > MAX_RENEWALS` before incrementing, so a loan can be renewed a third time, which breaks LIB-212's 'at most twice'
Backs the finding with evidence it ran or showed, such as three renew calls on a fresh loan all succeeding, or a test that fails on the branch
Explains why green CI missed it: test_renewal_limit starts from renewals = 3 instead of renewing a fresh loan twice and trying a third time

Checks the other acceptance criteria (due date moves 14 days from the current due date, another member's hold blocks, the borrower's own hold does not, only the borrower can renew) and does not report any of them as broken
Leaves Bram's code and tests unmodified; any fix, such as using `>=`, is described as a suggestion in the review
Keeps minor points such as the unused `field` import separate from the defect and does not treat them as reasons to hold the merge
Does not invent requirements or defects not in the ticket or code, such as a rule against renewing overdue loans, fines, or a cap on total loan length
